title: FreqCa: Accelerating Image generation and Editing via Frequency-Aware Caching
claim: Our accelerated method still produces diverse, high-quality, detailed samples across styles and subjects, despite large speedups.
layout: Single collage mosaic of 13 varied-size images, centered title image
description: A dense mosaic of thirteen generated images tiled with white gutters and no axes, arrows or labels. The largest image sits at center-right: a bunny in a straw hat and green overalls holding a flowerpot among blooms, with the bubbly white text "FreqCa!" at the top. Around it are an expressionist oil portrait of a man, a giraffe close-up, an otter floating in a pond, a chameleon on colorful candy, a child sketching in an autumn park, a baroque flower still life, a Van Gogh-style self-portrait with a pipe, and an eagle close-up. Others show a whale in a coral forest, a fox in a glowing flower meadow, a woman's face among flowers, and a cartoon dragon flying past a pink castle. The eye goes first to the bunny and title, then to the vivid, varied styles.
caption: Images sampled by Qwen-image with FreqCa with 7.14× acceleration.
abstract: The application of diffusion transformers is suffering from their significant inference costs. Recently, feature caching has been proposed to solve this problem by reusing features from previous timesteps, thereby skipping computation in future timesteps. However, previous feature caching assumes that features in adjacent timesteps are similar or continuous, which does not always hold in all settings. To investigate this, this paper begins with an analysis from the frequency domain, which reveals that different frequency bands in the features of diffusion models exhibit different dynamics across timesteps. Concretely, low-frequency components, which decide the structure of images, exhibit higher similarity but poor continuity. In contrast, the high-frequency bands, which decode the details of images, show significant continuity but poor similarity. These interesting observations motivate us to propose Frequency-aware Caching (FreqCa) which directly reuses features of low-frequency components based on their similarity, while using a second-order Hermite interpolator to predict the volatile high-frequency ones based on their continuity. Besides, we further propose to cache Cumulative Residual Feature (CRF) instead of the features in all the layers, which reduces the memory footprint of feature caching by 99%. Extensive experiments on FLUX.1-dev, FLUX.1-Kontext-dev, Qwen-Image, and Qwen-Image-Edit demonstrate its effectiveness in both generation and editing. Our codes have been released in Github: https://github.com/Tammytcl/FreqCa
